Your Grace,

Overall: the plan is solid and aligns with Vue Flow’s built-in nesting and ELK’s hierarchical handling. It will deliver exactly what you asked: packages contain modules; modules contain classes/interfaces; no containment edges; parents auto-resize; children constrained to parent bounds.

### Strengths
- Native Vue Flow nesting via parentNode/extent enables true containment and drag grouping, matching the official nesting example.
- Removing containment edges avoids artificial layering constraints; hierarchy becomes visual, not edge-driven.
- ELK direction mapping and hierarchical config improve layout readability for real dependency edges.

### Small adjustments to ensure smooth adoption
- Keep data.parentId temporarily for compatibility while switching to parentNode; remove later once no longer referenced.
- Ensure we only map LR/RL/TB/BT to RIGHT/LEFT/DOWN/UP once (either in the processor or worker). Avoid double-mapping.
- Keep edges for real relationships (imports, inheritance, implements) only; fully drop “contains” edges to meet your constraint.

### Risks and mitigations
- Parent sizing vs. ELK positions: minor drift can occur until sizes settle. Mitigation: two-pass layout (initial default size, then re-run after measurement) as you already noted.
- Very dense graphs may still create long chains given true dependencies. Mitigation: spacing controls and potential future edge bundling.

### Acceptance criteria (quick)
- Packages visually contain modules; modules contain classes/interfaces.
- Parents auto-expand as children move; children stay within bounds.
- No containment edges rendered; dependency edges still route well.
- Direction controls yield correct LR/RL/TB/BT orientation.
